=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/worktree_registry.sh:134 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `git -C "${repo_root}" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null | PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 - "${repo_root}" "${created_at}" <<'PY'` construct combines a shell pipe with a heredoc on the same command. The heredoc overrides the piped stdin, so the Python process receives the heredoc script body on stdin instead of the git worktree porcelain output.
  WHY: The worktree registry parser (`sys.stdin.read()`) reads the Python script body instead of git output, so the registry entry list is always empty or malformed. Any caller that depends on the worktree registry for GC or lifecycle tracking will operate on stale or empty data. The CI lint job (`shellcheck --severity=error scripts/*.sh`) fails hard on this line, blocking the PR merge.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:278 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `inject_after_offset` strips only `"\n"` from the remainder (`remainder = rendered_text[paragraph_end:].lstrip("\n")`) while `opening_role_goal_end_offset` computes offsets using `raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")`. For CRLF files the remainder could start with a stray `"\r"`.
  WHY: The injected output would contain mixed line endings and formatting artifacts (stray carriage return characters in the rendered prompt). In practice this repo uses LF line endings so the runtime impact is minimal, but the asymmetry is a real defect in the logic.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/worktree_registry.sh:134 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Shellcheck SC2259 error - the heredoc `<<'PY'` overrides the piped input from `git worktree list --porcelain`. The Python script receives the heredoc content instead of the git worktree list output, breaking registry parsing.
  WHY: The pipe `|` feeds stdin to the command, but `<<'PY'` also provides stdin. Shellcheck reports this as an error because the heredoc overrides the pipe, so `sys.stdin.read()` in the Python script sees the script body instead of the porcelain output.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:277 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: CRLF handling asymmetry - `opening_role_goal_end_offset` calculates offsets using `raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")` but `inject_after_offset()` only strips `"\n"` when processing remainder. If a prompt file has Windows line endings (CRLF), the remainder could start with a stray `"\r"`, causing formatting artifacts in the injected output.
  WHY: When processing a prompt file with CRLF line endings, the calculated paragraph_end accounts for both `\r` and `\n`, but the remainder only strips `\n`, leaving a leading `\r` that creates malformed output.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/worktree_registry.sh:134 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `git worktree list --porcelain` output is piped into `python3 -`, but the `<<'PY'` heredoc overrides stdin, so `sys.stdin.read()` gets the heredoc body (the Python source itself) instead of the git worktree porcelain lines. The Python script reads `sys.stdin` starting from its own source code text, which will not parse as porcelain output. The Python `-` flag reads stdin as the script to execute, but the heredoc redirects stdin to the Python body, so `sys.stdin.read().splitlines()` iterates over the Python source code rather than the git worktree output. This means the worktree list is never consumed from the pipe.
  WHY: The pipe delivers porcelain output to fd 0, but the heredoc immediately remaps fd 0 to the script text, so the Python program reads its own source code as `sys.stdin` input instead of the git porcelain data. Every `_worktree_registry_rebuild_json` call produces an empty entries array because no lines in the heredoc match porcelain keys.
- scripts/render_prompt.sh:276-278 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `inject_after_offset` strips only `\n` from the remainder (`lstrip("\n")`), but `opening_role_goal_end_offset` computes the offset using `raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")`. For CRLF-encoded prompt files, the remainder will start with a stray `\r` character, producing injected output with mixed line endings.
  WHY: `lstrip("\r\n")` strips both characters; `lstrip("\n")` only strips `\n`. A CRLF prompt file will get `\r` at the start of the remainder, so the identity block will be separated from the role/goal paragraph by `\n\n\r` instead of `\n\n\n`, and the remainder text will have a leading `\r`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
